title: Burst Admission SLOs, Error Budgets, and Alerting (Redwood Dedicated Burst)
author: Aisha Bello
body:
h1. Purpose
This page defines the production SLOs, error budgets, and alert thresholds for *Burst Capacity* in Redwood Dedicated. The goals are:

* Keep burst behavior predictable for Dedicated customers (fast, deterministic admission decisions).
* Protect other tenants and the hosted fleet via strict guardrails (noisy-neighbor protection).
* Make incidents involving burst straightforward to classify and respond to.

This document is used by SRE, Routing, Fleet, and Telemetry teams as the source-of-truth for on-call expectations and alert tuning.

----

h1. Scope
This page covers:

* *Burst Admission* path: baseline → burst eligibility evaluation → burst pool routing → fallback/deny.
* *Neighbor Protection* signals: dedicated baseline SLOs, pool saturation, and tail-latency drift correlated with burst.
* Alerting for burst-specific failure modes (misconfig, saturation, policy/routing bugs).
* Incident classification when burst is a contributing factor.

Out of scope:

* General Dedicated baseline SLOs (covered elsewhere).
* Pricing/billing correctness SLOs (shadow metering is tracked separately during pilot).
* Spot/preemptible burst semantics (v1 is strict admission control; no preemption guarantees).

----

h1. Definitions and terminology
* *Baseline capacity:* the customer’s reserved Dedicated pool (contracted throughput).
* *Burst capacity:* temporary capacity sourced from controlled shared burst pools, subject to hard caps and cooldowns.
* *Burst-eligible request:* a request that (a) is for a burst-enabled tenant, (b) is within configured tenant guardrails, and (c) targets an eligible region/GPU pool.
* *Admission decision:* the *policy outcome* returned to Routing for a request: {baseline, burst_allowed, burst_denied, fallback_allowed, hard_deny}.
* *Neighbor:* any other workload that could be impacted by contention (other Dedicated tenants, hosted fleet commitments, or other burst-enabled tenants in shared burst pools).

Key reason codes (used in logs/metrics; safe subset exposed to customers):

* LIMIT_TPS_EXCEEDED
* LIMIT_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED
* COOLDOWN_ACTIVE
* POOL_SATURATION_GATE
* REGION_NOT_ELIGIBLE
* CONFIG_INVALID_OR_MISSING
* POLICY_EVAL_ERROR

----

h1. SLIs and SLOs
SLOs are defined at two layers:

1) *Customer experience of burst admission* (fast, predictable decisioning and appropriate responses)
2) *Platform safety / neighbor protection* (burst must not materially degrade baseline guarantees)

Unless otherwise stated, SLOs are evaluated per region and aggregated across all burst-enabled tenants. During pilot, we additionally watch per-tenant burn to catch misconfigurations early.

h2. SLI 1 — Admission decision availability
*Intent:* Policy + routing can make an admission decision without errors.

*SLI definition:*

AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate = (count of requests with a non-error admission decision) / (count of burst-eligible admission attempts)

*Inclusions:* burst-eligible admission attempts (requests that reach the admission evaluation stage).

*Exclusions:* requests that never reach admission evaluation because the tenant is not burst-enabled.

*SLO target:*

* 99.95% over 30 days (GA)
* 99.9% over 30 days (Pilot)

*Error budget policy:* Burn is attributed to the owning component:

* POLICY_EVAL_ERROR → Control Plane / Policy Service on-call
* Routing unable to apply admission outcome → Smart Routing on-call

h2. SLI 2 — Admission decision latency
*Intent:* Admission should be fast enough to not add meaningful overhead on the request path.

*SLI definition:*

AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 = p99(latency from Routing admission request to decision applied)

*SLO target:*

* p99 ≤ 25ms over 7 days (GA)
* p99 ≤ 40ms over 7 days (Pilot)

Notes:

* This SLO is measured at Routing (end-to-end) and includes policy cache hits/misses.
* A sustained increase often indicates policy cache invalidation loops, control plane slowness, or routing retries.

h2. SLI 3 — Burst admission correctness (guardrail enforcement)
*Intent:* When configured limits say “deny,” the system must deny. This is a *safety SLO*.

*SLI definition (audited):*

GuardrailBypassRate = (count of requests admitted to burst that violate hard limits at decision time) / (count of burst-admitted requests)

Hard limits include max_concurrency and max_tokens_per_second (TPS) at the tenant+region scope.

*SLO target:*

* ≤ 0.001% over 30 days (GA)
* ≤ 0.01% over 30 days (Pilot)

Measurement approach:

* Primary: policy decision logs with signed decision context (tenant, region, evaluated counters).
* Secondary: reconciliation using telemetry counters (shadow metering + concurrency trackers).

Any non-zero sustained bypass is treated as Sev-2 minimum (see incident section).

h2. SLI 4 — Burst pool saturation gate health
*Intent:* Burst pools should apply saturation gates to protect neighbors (deny early instead of degrading everyone).

*SLI definition:*

PoolSaturationGateEffectiveness = 1 - (count of “admitted to burst” while pool is above saturation threshold) / (count of burst-admitted requests)

“Saturation threshold” is defined per pool (GPU type, region) and is set by Fleet; see design spec for thresholds and headroom logic.

*SLO target:*

* ≥ 99.9% over 30 days (GA)
* ≥ 99.5% over 30 days (Pilot)

h2. SLI 5 — Neighbor protection: baseline latency integrity
*Intent:* Enabling burst must not materially degrade baseline Dedicated performance.

We define a burst-related “neighbor harm” SLI based on p99 drift on baseline traffic when burst utilization is high.

*SLI definition:*

BaselineP99Drift = (baseline p99 latency during burst_high windows) / (baseline p99 latency during burst_low windows)

Where:

* burst_high windows: burst pool utilization ≥ 80% for ≥ 10 minutes
* burst_low windows: burst pool utilization ≤ 30%

*SLO target (per region):*

* BaselineP99Drift ≤ 1.10 over 7 days (GA)
* BaselineP99Drift ≤ 1.15 over 7 days (Pilot)

Notes and caveats:

* We do not page directly on drift alone (can be workload mix). Drift triggers investigation when correlated with burst saturation and increased burst admit rates.
* For Dedicated baseline SLO violations, severity is driven by the baseline SLO, not by burst.

----

h1. Error budgets and policy
h2. Error budget consumption
We track error budget for:

* AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate (Availability)
* AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 (Latency)
* GuardrailBypassRate (Safety)
* PoolSaturationGateEffectiveness (Safety)

Guidance:

* *Safety SLOs (guardrail bypass, saturation gating)* have a “near-zero” tolerance. Any measurable sustained regression requires immediate mitigation (tighten gates, disable burst for a tenant/region) before root-cause completion.
* *Availability/latency SLOs* follow standard burn-rate alerting (below) and can be addressed with mitigations and follow-up work if within budget.

h2. Launch gates tied to error budgets
* Pilot → expanded pilot: two consecutive weeks with:

  * AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate ≥ 99.9%
  * GuardrailBypassRate = 0 (observed)
  * No Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents attributable to burst

* Expanded pilot → GA readiness: 30 days with:

  * AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate ≥ 99.95%
  * AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 ≤ 25ms (7-day rolling)
  * GuardrailBypassRate ≤ 0.001%
  * BaselineP99Drift ≤ 1.10 in all GA regions (or documented exceptions + mitigation)

----

h1. Alerting
Alerts are grouped into:

* *Paging (on-call)*: potential customer impact or safety issue requiring immediate action.
* *Ticket/Slack (non-paging)*: requires triage in business hours.

Unless stated, alerts are evaluated per region; paging routes to #oncall-sre and the relevant component on-call (Routing, Fleet, Platform).

h2. Paging alerts
1) *Burst admission availability burn (fast)*

*Condition:* AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate drops below 99.0% over 5 minutes for any GA region.

*Rationale:* Indicates policy eval errors, dependency outages, or routing integration failure.

*Primary action:* Follow runbook “Burst Admission Failures” (see runbook index; interim actions include disabling burst flag per tenant or per region).

2) *Policy/routing error spike tied to admission*

*Condition:* POLICY_EVAL_ERROR reason code rate > 0.5% of burst-eligible attempts for 10 minutes.

*Rationale:* Often indicates config schema/migration issues, cache poisoning, or policy service regression.

*Primary action:* Roll back recent changes; flip “force_baseline_only” override for impacted tenants.

3) *Guardrail bypass detected (safety)*

*Condition:* GuardrailBypassRate > 0 in any 10-minute window OR > 0.001% over 1 hour.

*Rationale:* This is a safety defect. Immediate mitigation is mandatory.

*Primary action:* Disable burst for the tenant/region and engage Control Plane + Routing DRIs.

4) *Burst pool saturation with baseline risk*

*Condition:* Burst pool utilization ≥ 90% for 15 minutes AND (baseline p99 latency +15% vs trailing 24h median OR baseline error rate +0.5%) in the same region.

*Rationale:* Saturation alone is expected during spikes; paging occurs only when correlated with baseline risk.

*Primary action:* Execute saturation runbook: tighten tenant limits, enable cooldown, shift pool weight, or disable burst for top offenders.

h2. Non-paging alerts (ticket/Slack)
1) *Burst deny surge (customer experience)*

*Condition:* BurstDeniedRate ≥ 20% of burst-eligible attempts for 30 minutes (per tenant OR per region).

*Rationale:* Usually indicates misconfigured limits, unexpected traffic shape, or insufficient pool headroom.

*Action:* Create ticket for Dedicated Success + Capacity Planning; propose limit adjustments or pool sizing changes.

2) *Admission latency regression*

*Condition:* AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 > 25ms for 2 hours (GA) or > 40ms (Pilot).

*Action:* Investigate cache hit rate, policy dependency latency, routing retries.

3) *Cooldown thrash indicator*

*Condition:* COOLDOWN_ACTIVE denies > 10% of burst-eligible attempts for 1 hour.

*Rationale:* Suggests limits too tight or cooldown parameters too aggressive; can cause customer-visible oscillation.

*Action:* Tune cooldown parameters (Fleet + SRE), validate with canary.

----

h1. Incident classification (when burst is involved)
We classify incidents by *customer impact* first, then by *contributing component*. Burst-related incidents follow normal severity definitions but have special tags and escalation rules.

h2. Required incident tags
For any incident where burst is suspected or confirmed as a factor, include:

* tag: dedicated_burst
* tag: burst_pool_<region> (e.g., burst_pool_us-east-1)
* tag: component_<routing|policy|fleet|telemetry>

h2. Severity guidelines
*Sev-1 (customer-impacting outage / major degradation)*

* Dedicated baseline SLO violated for multiple tenants or a large enterprise tenant, and burst is a contributing factor (e.g., misrouted traffic to burst pools impacts baseline).
* Widespread admission failures causing elevated 5xx on Dedicated traffic during a traffic spike.

*Sev-2 (safety or significant customer harm)*

* Any confirmed guardrail bypass that admits traffic beyond hard limits.
* Any cross-tenant impact indicating noisy-neighbor behavior attributable to burst pools.
* Burst admission/routing bug causing incorrect fallback (e.g., routing to wrong region contrary to residency constraints).

*Sev-3 (limited scope / degradations with mitigation)*

* Elevated burst denials for one tenant due to pool headroom; baseline unaffected.
* Admission latency regression without clear customer impact.

h2. “Burst involved” post-incident requirements
For Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents with burst involved, the postmortem must include:

* Timeline of burst pool utilization, admit/deny rates, and top tenants by burst usage.
* Admission reason-code breakdown.
* Confirmation of whether saturation gate behaved as designed.
* Mitigations used (limit changes, cooldown toggles, disable commands) and effectiveness.
* Follow-up actions: (a) guardrail hardening, (b) alert tuning, (c) documentation/customer comms if error semantics were confusing.

----

h1. Operational notes
h2. Where to look (dashboards)
Primary dashboard set (Grafana): “Dedicated → Burst Capacity”

Recommended panels during an event:

* AdmissionDecisionSuccessRate (region)
* AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 (region)
* BurstAdmit / BurstDeny counts (region + tenant top-N)
* Deny reason codes (stacked)
* Burst pool utilization + saturation gates
* Baseline p99 latency overlayed with burst utilization

h2. Common failure modes mapped to SLOs
* Policy service outage → SLI 1 fails (admission availability), SLI 2 regresses (latency)
* Misconfigured limits (too low) → BurstDeniedRate spikes, possible cooldown thrash
* Routing regression (baseline → burst ordering incorrect) → baseline p99 drift and/or increased baseline errors
* Fleet headroom shortage → increased POOL_SATURATION_GATE denies; may be acceptable if baseline protected

----

h1. Ownership and change management
* SLO owner: *Eng-SRE* (DRI: Aisha Bello)
* Primary operational responders: *SRE on-call* + component on-call (Routing/Platform/Fleet)
* Changes to SLO targets or paging thresholds require:

  1. Review from SRE lead (Sean Gallagher)
  2. Sign-off from Routing lead (Mina Haddad) for routing-path metrics
  3. Sign-off from Fleet lead (Vanessa Ortiz) for saturation thresholds

All changes must be announced in #eng-sre and captured as a short changelog entry at the bottom of this page.

----

h1. Changelog
* 2025-08-22: Tightened GA AdmissionDecisionLatencyP99 target to 25ms; clarified guardrail bypass paging condition; added baseline-risk correlation requirement for saturation paging.
* 2025-07-14: Initial published SLOs/alerts for burst pilot and GA readiness.
